problems.title: An irrational input with rational output
problems.question: Which listed irrational $a$ makes $(a^a)^a$ rational?
problems.idea: Use the definitions and geometric relations, showing each substitution.
steps: Take $a=\sqrt2$. Then $a^2=2$ and $(a^a)^a=(\sqrt2)^2=2$, rational.

problems.title: Compare logarithms with different bases
problems.question: Solve $\log_4(x+7)>\log_2(x+1)$.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and geometric relations, showing each substitution.
steps: The domain is $x>-1$. Multiply by 2 and combine logarithms: $\log_2(x+7)>\log_2((x+1)^2)$.
As base 2 is increasing, $x+7>(x+1)^2$, or $(x+3)(x-2)<0$. Intersect $(-3,2)$ with the domain.

problems.title: An exponential inequality
problems.question: Solve $2^x\ge3^x$.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and geometric relations, showing each substitution.
steps: The base $2/3$ is between 0 and 1. Its power is at least 1 exactly when the exponent is nonpositive.

problems.title: Equal cylinder, cone and sphere volumes
problems.question: A cylinder, cone and sphere have radius 3 and equal volumes. Find the product of the cylinder and cone heights.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and geometric relations, showing each substitution.
steps: The common volume is $36\pi$. Hence $9\pi h=36\pi$ gives $h=4$, and $3\pi H=36\pi$ gives $H=12$.
The product is $4\cdot12=48$.

problems.title: A regular triangular pyramid
problems.question: The base is an equilateral triangle of side 6, and a lateral face makes $30^\circ$ with the base plane. Find volume.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and geometric relations, showing each substitution.
steps: $\rho=\sqrt3$, so $h=1$. The base area is $6^2\sqrt3/4=9\sqrt3$.
The volume is $9\sqrt3/3=3\sqrt3$.

problems.title: Cylinder around a regular hexagonal prism
problems.question: Every edge of a regular hexagonal prism is 1. Find the volume of its circumscribed cylinder.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and geometric relations, showing each substitution.
formulas: A regular hexagon’s circumradius equals its side; $V=\pi R^2h$.
steps: The cylinder radius and height are both 1. Therefore its volume is $\pi$.

problems.title: Count integer logarithmic solutions
problems.question: How many integers solve $\log_3x+\log_{\sqrt3}x+\log_{1/3}x<6$?
problems.idea: Use the definitions and geometric relations, showing each substitution.
steps: The inequality is $2t<6$, so $x<27$. The domain requires $x>0$.
The integers 1 through 26 give 26 solutions.

problems.title: An interval length determines the logarithm base
problems.question: For which $a$ does $\sqrt{\log_ax}\ge\log_ax$ have a solution interval of length 199?
problems.idea: Use the definitions and geometric relations, showing each substitution.
steps: For $a>1$, the interval is $[1,a]$, of length $a-1$. This equals 199 exactly for $a=200$.
For $0<a<1$, the interval is $[a,1]$, of length $1-a<1$, so it cannot work. Invalid bases $a\le0$ or $a=1$ are excluded.

problems.title: Length of a logarithmic solution interval
problems.question: Find the length of the solution interval of $(1-\log_4x)/(1-\log_8x)<0$.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and geometric relations, showing each substitution.
steps: Its numerator and denominator have opposite signs exactly when $2<t<3$.
Thus $4<x<8$, an interval of length 4.

problems.title: Apothem of a square-pyramid frustum
problems.question: Height and the two base sides have ratio $2:1:4$. Volume is 112. Find the apothem.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and geometric relations, showing each substitution.
steps: Write $h=2k,a=k,b=4k$. Then $V=14k^3=112$, so $k=2$.
The dimensions are $h=4,a=2,b=8$. Hence $l=\sqrt{4^2+3^2}=5$.

problems.title: A product of signs for natural inputs
problems.question: How many natural $x$ solve $(0.9^x-1)\log_{1.1}x<0$?
problems.idea: Use the definitions and geometric relations, showing each substitution.
steps: The product is negative for every integer $x\ge2$. At 1 the logarithm is zero, so strictness excludes it.

problems.title: Infer the base direction from a known solution
problems.question: Count natural solutions of $\log_a(x^2-11x+30)\le\log_a(16-2x)$, knowing $x=3$ is a solution.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and geometric relations, showing each substitution.
formulas: At $x=3$, the arguments are 6 and 10; this comparison forces $a>1$.
steps: The domains require $(x-5)(x-6)>0$ and $x<8$. Since the base is increasing, also require $x^2-11x+30\le16-2x$, or $(x-2)(x-7)\le0$.
The solution is $[2,5)\cup(6,7]$. Its natural inputs are $2,3,4,7$.

problems.title: Compare powers with one
problems.question: For the three powers $a,b,c$ printed in the source, determine which exceed 1.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and geometric relations, showing each substitution.
formulas: If $0<u<1$, then $u^v>1$ iff $v<0$; if $u>1$, then $u^v>1$ iff $v>0$.
steps: The base of $a$ is $(\sqrt{17}+3)/8<1$ and its exponent $\log_{199}0.1<0$, so $a>1$.
The base of $b$ is $\sqrt{17}-3>1$ and its exponent $\log_{19.9}0.1<0$, so $b<1$.
The base of $c$ is $(\sqrt{17}-3)/8<1$ and exponent $-\log_{1.99}0.1>0$, so $c<1$.

problems.title: An inscribed cone and its pyramid
problems.question: A cone and pyramid have a common apex; the cone base is the pyramid base’s incircle. If base perimeter divided by circle circumference is $k$, find pyramid-to-cone volume ratio.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and geometric relations, showing each substitution.
formulas: The common height cancels; polygon base area $=Pr/2$.
steps: The volume ratio is $(Pr/2)/(\pi r^2)=P/(2\pi r)$. This equals the given ratio $k$.

problems.title: Rotate a triangle about an exterior altitude
problems.question: An isosceles triangle with sides $2,2,2\sqrt3$ rotates about the line containing the altitude to an equal side. Find the solid volume.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and geometric relations, showing each substitution.
steps: Put the equal side on $AB$ with $A=(0,0),B=(2,0)$ and third vertex $C=(-1,\sqrt3)$. The included angle at $A$ is $120^\circ$, and the rotation axis is $x=-1$.
The rotated region is a cone of radius 3 and height $\sqrt3$ with a cone of radius 1 and the same height removed. At each height, both radii shrink in the same linear proportion.
The volume is $(\pi\sqrt3/3)(9-1)=8\pi/\sqrt3$.

problems.title: First decimal digit of a logarithm
problems.question: Find the first digit after the decimal point of $\log_{10}2$.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and geometric relations, showing each substitution.
steps: The first digit after the decimal point is 3.

problems.title: Integer lattice points with logarithms
problems.question: Count integer pairs satisfying $\log_2|x|+\log_2|y|<2$ and $x^2+y^2>5$.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and geometric relations, showing each substitution.
steps: Possible positive absolute pairs are $(1,1),(1,2),(2,1),(1,3),(3,1)$.
Only $(1,3)$ and $(3,1)$ have squared sum strictly greater than 5. Each allows four sign combinations, giving eight points.

problems.title: A frustum volume from two sphere volumes
problems.question: Two sphere volumes are $V,W$. A cone frustum has their radii as base radii and height equal to the radii’s difference. Find its volume.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and geometric relations, showing each substitution.
steps: Take $R\ge r$, so $h=R-r$. Then $V_f=\pi(R^3-r^3)/3$.
The difference of sphere volumes is $4\pi(R^3-r^3)/3$. Thus the frustum volume is $|V-W|/4$.

problems.title: A plane bisects a tetrahedron’s volume
problems.question: $SA_1:A_1A=SB_1:B_1B=3:1$. A plane through $A_1,B_1,C_1$ halves tetrahedron $SABC$. Find $SC_1:C_1C$.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and geometric relations, showing each substitution.
formulas: Tetrahedra sharing an apex have volume ratio equal to the product of the three edge fractions.
steps: Let $t=SC_1/SC$. The small tetrahedron volume fraction is $(3/4)(3/4)t=1/2$.
Thus $t=8/9$, leaving fraction $1/9$, so the requested ratio is $8:1$.

problems.title: A rational number between two logarithms
problems.question: Which listed number lies in $(\log_35,\log_23)$?
problems.idea: Use the definitions and geometric relations, showing each substitution.
steps: $25<27$ proves the first inequality after squaring; $8<9$ proves the second.
Hence $3/2$ lies strictly between the bounds.

problems.title: When a radical inequality has no solutions
problems.question: Find $a$ for which $(x-a)\sqrt{3\cdot2^x-2\cdot3^x}>0$ has no solution.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and geometric relations, showing each substitution.
formulas: For a strictly positive product with a square root, require positive radicand and $x>a$.
steps: The radicand is positive iff $(3/2)^x<3/2$, or $x<1$. At $x=1$ the product is zero and is not allowed.
The solution interval is $(a,1)$ if $a<1$, and empty if $a\ge1$.

problems.title: Equal numerical volume and surface area
problems.question: A right square prism has base side $a$ metres. Its volume in cubic metres equals its total area in square metres. Which $a$ are possible?
problems.idea: Use the definitions and geometric relations, showing each substitution.
steps: Equate numerical values: $h(a^2-4a)=2a^2$, so $h=2a/(a-4)$.
With $a>0$, this height is positive exactly when $a>4$. Every such $a$ gives a valid height.

problems.title: Largest integer solution of a power inequality
problems.question: Find the greatest integer satisfying $((\sqrt{17}+3)/8)^{x/(1-x)}<(\sqrt{17}-3)^{x/(x+2)}$.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and geometric relations, showing each substitution.
steps: The left base is $1/b$, so the inequality becomes $x/(x-1)<x/(x+2)$, with $x\ne1,-2$.
It is equivalent to $3x/[(x-1)(x+2)]<0$. A sign chart gives $(-\infty,-2)\cup(0,1)$.
The greatest integer in this set is $-3$.

problems.title: A tetrahedron with congruent isosceles faces
problems.question: Every face of a triangular pyramid has sides 5,5,6. Find its volume.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and geometric relations, showing each substitution.
formulas: A disphenoid can have vertices $(u,v,w),(u,-v,-w),(-u,v,-w),(-u,-v,w)$; its volume is $8uvw/3$.
steps: Opposite edges of length 6 give $v^2+w^2=9$. The two other edge pairs of length 5 give $u^2+v^2=u^2+w^2=25/4$.
Thus $v^2=w^2=9/2$, $u^2=7/4$. With positive coordinates, $uvw=9\sqrt7/4$.
The determinant volume is $8uvw/3=6\sqrt7$.

problems.title: Distances from a circumsphere centre to pyramid faces
problems.question: A regular square pyramid has base side 2 and lateral edge $\sqrt{17}$. Find the sum of distances from its circumsphere centre to all five faces.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and geometric relations, showing each substitution.
formulas: Equal distances to vertices determine the sphere centre; point-to-plane distance is $|ax+by+cz-d|/\sqrt{a^2+b^2+c^2}$.
steps: Put base vertices at $(\pm1,\pm1,0)$ and apex at $(0,0,H)$. Then $H=\sqrt{17-2}=\sqrt{15}$. Let the sphere centre be $(0,0,c)$.
Equality of squared vertex distances gives $(H-c)^2=c^2+2$, so $c=13/(2\sqrt{15})$. This is the base-plane distance.
A lateral face has equation $Hy+z=H$ and normal length $\sqrt{H^2+1}=4$. Its distance from the centre is $(H-c)/4=17/(8\sqrt{15})$.
Add all five distances: $c+4(H-c)/4=H=\sqrt{15}$.
